correct.text: The hovercraft reached the beach at dawn.

statement: An ing-marked verbal dependent commonly identifies the intended use of the object named by the noun head.

correct.text: He packed a walking stick for the ridge trail.

statement: A bahuvrihi denotes an entity characterized by the property expressed by its component bases, which begin with an adjective or a noun.
condition: This small productive group often describes people derogatorily and can occur in vocatives. It also includes animal, plant and inanimate referents.

correct.text: A redbreast hopped onto the wall.
She packed her groceries into the hatchback.

correct.text: That lazybones is still asleep on the sofa.

statement: The initial noun can correspond to a subject, an object or a prepositional complement in a related clause.

correct.text: A cloudburst flooded the path.

condition: The interpretation is generally narrower than for noun plus noun compounds without a verbal centre.

correct.text: The window cleaner rang the bell.

concept: Plural marking in established er plus preposition compounds
statement: In established compounds such as passer-by and runner-up, plural inflection attaches to the er head before the final preposition.
condition: The intended noun is the standard compound passer-by or runner-up, and its syntax or meaning requires a plural.
violation: The plural ending follows the final preposition instead of the noun head.

exceptions.description: The final-s restriction is specific to the listed lexemes. Initial-preposition compounds inflect their final noun head. Nonstandard nonce forms with two er suffixes can also take a final plural ending.

correct.text: Two passers-by helped push the van.
The runners-up each received a medal.

incorrect.text: Two passer-bys helped push the van.

diagnostic.error_pattern: Plural suffix follows by or up in the standard compound noun passer-by or runner-up.

concept: Singular measure bases in attributive compounds
statement: A productive attributive compound formed from a numeral and a unit noun uses a singular noun base.
